item.title: Sexual and family violence against children at 'crisis point', study finds
item.description: Violence and sexual violence against children have increased sharply across Australia, research by the University of Sydney finds. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: NASA JPL testing readies Voyager technologies lander for moon mission
item.description: A commercial lander that will be at the forefront of NASA's efforts to establish a moon base, humanity's first lunar outpost, has passed a series of critical tests at the agency's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California. The tests simulated the extreme temperatures and vacuum of space, as well as the intense shaking and ear-splitting roar of launch. Results show that Voyager Technologies' Griffin Mission One (Griffin-1) spacecraft is ready to survive the rigors of space exploration. Publicado también por: NASA. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Chemical surroundings, not size alone, help glucose-processing enzyme stay active as temperatures rise
item.description: Cells must produce energy despite changing conditions. But what keeps metabolic enzymes functional during temperature fluctuations? A team led by professor Simon Ebbinghaus and Dr. Harshita Rastogi at Ruhr University Bochum and the Research Center for Chemical Sciences and Sustainability investigated this question using the platelet isoform of phosphofructokinase-1 (PFKP), a central enzyme in glucose metabolism. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Americans are stressed about grocery prices, so why do they toss or overlook so much 'misfit' food?
item.description: There's a paradox that drives the shopping decisions of many Americans: Almost three-quarters say they're feeling stressed out about skyrocketing grocery bills. But they keep discarding large quantities of food that's safe to eat, from crooked carrots to surplus yogurt to "best before" items pulled from shelves early. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Natural RNA modifications in archaea mirror those used in medicine
item.description: RNA therapeutics open up new possibilities for the targeted and precise treatment of diseases. To ensure that RNA molecules remain stable in the body and can reliably exert their effects, they undergo specific chemical modifications. However, such modifications to the RNA backbone also occur naturally, according to research by Schraga Schwartz, a professor at the Weizmann Institute of Science (Rehovot, Israel), and Dr. Dina Grohmann, a professor at the University of Regensburg. Their research findings have now been published in the journal Cell under the title "Phosphate backbone… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Winged insect evolution: New evidence sheds light on century-old debate
item.description: A new study combining genomic analyses and fossil evidence sheds light on the century-old "Palaeoptera Problem," a longstanding debate over the evolutionary relationships among major groups of winged insects. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Forget rockets — Longshot wants to fire cargo into space from a gun. See it at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
item.description: Longshot is trying to build a gun big enough to make space data centers a reality. Fuente: TechCrunch.
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz

item.title: Variations in the human vocal tract could have influenced language diversity
item.description: The anatomical differences in our vocal tracts could be one of the sources of our Tower of Babel—the vast difference in languages spoken around the world, according to a study published in the open-access journal PLOS Biology by Steven Moran and Tiena Danner from the University of Neuchâtel, Switzerland, and colleagues. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Messy, risky outdoor play is important for children, but adults can stop them enjoying it
item.description: There is growing evidence that children today have fewer opportunities for independent, adventurous outdoor play and fewer chances to make decisions and shape their own experiences than previous generations. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Description This infographic illustrates the distances driven by various rovers on the surface of Earth’s Moon and Mars. Of the vehicles shown, the NASA Mars rovers Perseverance and Curiosity are still operational and moving across the surface; the figures shown for those two are distances driven as of Oct. 11, 2026. As of that date, […] Fuente: NASA.

item.description: Description Members of NASA’s Perseverance Mars mission team gather in the Mars Yard at the agency’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California with a certificate from Guinness World Records marking the rover distance record on the Red Planet. Positioned in front of the team is OPTIMISM (Operational Perseverance Twin for Integration of Mechanisms and Instruments […] Fuente: NASA.

item.description: Description Rover tracks and a rocky Martian landscape are shown in this image captured by one of the navigation cameras (navcams) aboard NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover on Oct. 11, 2026, the 2,006th Martian day, or sol, of the mission. During that sol’s drive, spanning 299.6 feet (91.31 meters), the mission passed a major milestone: pushing Perseverance’s total […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: 'Atmospheric rivers' helped open a Portugal-sized hole in Antarctica's winter sea ice
item.description: Polynyas are patches of open water surrounded by sea ice, where heat and moisture can pass freely between the ocean and atmosphere. In August 2024, a vast polynya opened up in Breid Bay, off the coast of East Antarctica, in the depths of winter. The region had stayed ice-covered at this time of year ever since satellite records began in 1979. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Three NASA-supported small spacecraft, along with many commercial payloads, are shown before being encapsulated in a SpaceX Falcon 9 ahead of launch on Oct. 1, 2026. item.title: New solar model maps sun more accurately by checking far-side activity
item.description: A Southwest Research Institute (SwRI)-led team has developed an improved model for predicting solar events that incorporates activity on the far side of the sun. The team studied near-simultaneous maps of the whole solar surface from 2010 to 2014, combining Earth observations with data from space-based assets showing the opposite side. The resulting framework constructs surface flux transport (SFT) models that are more complete and accurate than any previous model. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How literature can inspire us to forgive
item.description: A story that places us inside the mind of a character who is remorseful about causing harm can inspire forgiveness for that fictional bad act, a new study finds. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Voyager Technologies’ Griffin-1 Completes Environmental Testing at NASA JPL
item.description: Description A lunar lander from Voyager Technologies completed nearly three months of environmental testing at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California in late September 2026. The tests demonstrate that the spacecraft is prepared to face the harsh conditions of launch, its journey to the Moon, and landing on the surface. Its final trial was […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Sexual violence survivors often expect systems to fail or harm them, study finds
item.description: University students who are survivors of sexual violence are forced to perform a constant, exhausting "calculus"—weighing risks, safety, stigma, emotional costs, institutional consequences and likelihood of being believed—when deciding whether and how to seek help. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A small RNA switch with huge potential opens up new possibilities for synthetic biology
item.description: An international research team led by TU Darmstadt Professor Beatrix Süß, working in close collaboration with partners in Germany and Denmark, has elucidated how an RNA switch newly developed at TU Darmstadt recognizes the antibiotic doxycycline and thereby selectively activates or deactivates gene expression. This makes doxycycline a promising basis for synthetic biology and, potentially, for gene therapies as well. The team recently published its findings in Nature Communications. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A closer look at hard-to-see cells could answer new questions about nerve damage and recovery
item.description: Under the microscope, mitochondria inside healthy terminal Schwann cells form a web of interconnected branches, with tiny doughnut-shaped loops appearing near where the cells branch and split. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 'Discovery compact' proposal calls for new social contract to sustain U.S. science
item.description: In a perspective article, Sergio Carbajo and colleagues call for a "Discovery Compact" in the face of the recent destabilization of the postwar compact for science, which reliably supported basic research for decades. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Nanoparticle injection reprograms NK immune cells to fight cancer and autoimmune disorders
item.description: MIT engineers have developed a new way to program natural killer (NK) immune cells to target cancerous T cells or T cells that have become autoreactive, leading to diseases such as lymphoma and autoimmune hepatitis. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Mushroom-derived peptides boost saltiness by up to 70%, offering a path to low-sodium foods
item.description: Scientists have found a way to make salt taste saltier without increasing its sodium content, a welcome development in the culinary world. Salt is a powerful flavor enhancer, drawing out the subtle flavors of a dish while balancing sweetness and bitterness. Its appeal comes hand in hand with some drawbacks. Salt activates the brain's reward system, making food more pleasurable, but eating too much salty food can negatively affect cardiovascular health. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Feeling undervalued emerges as strongest link to women leaving academia, survey finds
item.description: Women leave academia at higher rates than men, contributing to consistent gender imbalances at senior levels. Interventions often target work-life balance and motherhood. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A study unravels the genetic mystery of a cobra divided by sea
item.description: COLOMBO – Sri Lanka’s spectacled cobra (Naja naja) carries a two-million-year-old genetic mystery, and a new study finds that the island’s cobras form a genetically distinct lineage, reopening a taxonomic question raised by a Sri Lankan zoologist nearly nine decades ago. The study also established that the spectacled cobra has evolved from an African ancestor […] Fuente: Mongabay.
item.dc:creator: Dilrukshi Handunnetti

item.title: Powerful X-rays reveal unexpected roles for water in enzymes linked to cancer and penicillin
item.description: In biology, a group of enzymes called 2-oxoglutarate-dependent oxygenases is responsible for catalyzing a wide range of reactions that play a role in everything from how genetic code is used by cells to the synthesis of antibiotics. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Boys' lower regard for school effort may help explain academic gender gap
item.description: A survey of 15-year-olds around the world suggests that the underperformance of boys in education may be linked to gendered cultural attitudes about whether it is important to try hard at school. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Newly discovered 3D 'chair' shape can fill all space without repeating patterns
item.description: Software developer Ioannis Tsiokos has reported the discovery of a three-dimensional shape, which roughly resembles a chair, that can fill space infinitely without repeating a pattern. The shape follows certain mathematical rules that make it the first of its kind in three dimensions. The AI-assisted findings are described in an arXiv preprint paper. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Recycled fertilizers from sanitation systems are as effective as conventional fertilizers, study finds
item.description: Agriculture depends on a reliable supply of nutrients. Phosphorus, nitrogen and potassium, for example, are indispensable for agricultural crop production. However, natural reserves are limited, vary greatly in regional availability or are very energy-intensive to extract. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Structure in the unstructured: New phenomenon discovered in the solar wind
item.description: Turbulence is ubiquitous and occurs every day, such as when milk is stirred into coffee or in the stormy motions of the ocean and the atmosphere. Media in space and astrophysical systems can also develop turbulence, but the physics is different because the medium is in an ionized state (known as the plasma state) and the flow motion is strongly coupled to electromagnetic fields. Furthermore, space plasma is collisionless because the medium is so dilute that the particles do not collide with each other. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Copper-resistant bacteria complicate efforts to keep ship hulls clean
item.description: Marine bacteria have evolved to bypass the copper-based coatings applied to ship hulls to stop the growth of barnacles, algae and other marine life. This necessitates new methods for managing biofouling—the unwanted accumulation of marine organisms—on ship hulls. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How much training is too much for a racehorse? New bone research has some answers
item.description: The old "more is better" mindset in racehorse training is changing. And with no link identified between higher racehorse training workloads and a trainer's success, there's a big opportunity to change things. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Webb spots possible early-universe supernova just days after it happened
item.description: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has detected a possible supernova in the early universe just days after the star exploded. Called AT 2026abck, the transient lies in a star-forming galaxy at a redshift of 5.017 and was found without the help of gravitational lensing. JWST observations suggest the event was caught only about four to 10 days after the explosion. The paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Sept. 29. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Reaching net zero sooner could limit long-lasting El Niño-like shift in the Pacific
item.description: Reaching net zero sooner would limit long-lasting changes to El Niño and the tropical Pacific, new climate modeling suggests, although heat stored deep in the ocean means changes to the tropical Pacific could persist for centuries. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: What sets Gen-Z entrepreneurs apart from prior generations
item.description: Idealism, it's often thought, runs high at either end of the age spectrum and sags in the middle. The altruistic inclinations of youth are set aside due to the professional and personal demands of midlife but reemerge as one ages into maturity. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Mauritius, Seychelles among most capitalist nations in Africa according to new index
item.description: Mauritius, Seychelles and Botswana are the most capitalist countries in Africa, according to the Global Capitalism Index, a new ranking published by researchers affiliated with the University of Virginia. Fuente: Africanews.

item.description: Los investigadores emiratíes afirmaron que el copiloto acusado de agredir a un capitán en un vuelo con destino a Israel se fue inclinando hacia el extremismo durante su etapa como estudiante en Australia. Fuente: Clarín - Mundo.

item.title: Vera Rubin Observatory spots the largest ultra-fast spinning asteroid yet
item.description: The speed of an asteroid's spin can tell astronomers a surprising amount about what it is made of. However, existing approaches to measuring spin based on telescope observations can often produce misleading estimates. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Flexible work is everywhere—except where future leaders need it most
item.description: Employers could unlock a lucrative stream of talent by focusing their attention on "good flexibility," according to a new report. Bankwest Curtin Economics Center's analysis of the Workplace Gender Equality Agency's (WGEA) extensive employer dataset shows progress on gender equality has been made in the past decade, but workforce potential and opportunities to improve business performance remain untapped. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: James Webb reveals a massive cosmic structure that challenges our understanding of the Universe
item.description: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope has revealed an ancient galaxy cluster with an unexpectedly dense concentration of dark matter, challenging theories about how the universe developed. The discovery also uncovered a surprising connection between scattered starlight and invisible dark matter that could transform how astronomers study the early cosmos. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Why what we hate in music matters
item.description: Amanda Krause, a senior lecturer in psychology at James Cook University, said musical taste shapes social identity, personal expression and everyday behavior. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Science, Cargo Launch on 35th SpaceX Resupply Mission to Station
item.description: NASA’s SpaceX 35th commercial resupply mission lifted off at 6:33 a.m. EDT Tuesday aboard a Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, carrying more than 6,300 pounds of supplies and hardware, bound for the International Space Station. Following its successful launch, the SpaceX Dragon spacecraft will […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: 'Devastating' waves leave California beach homes on brink of collapse
item.description: Emergency repairs and cleanup were underway Monday in California's wave-battered city of Long Beach, where several homes appeared on the brink of collapse and remained too dangerous to enter. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Conor Shea sets a Guinness record by assembling Mr Potato Head blindfolded in 7.91 seconds
item.description: Conor Shea set a Guinness World Record on 7 February 2026 by assembling Mr Potato Head while blindfolded. His record time of 7.91 seconds was achieved in Louisville, Kentucky, USA. Shea aimed to raise awareness about Usher Syndrome, a genetic disorder causing hearing loss and blindness. Through this attempt, he demonstrated that people with the condition can achieve impressive goals. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Scientists discover a surprising paradox in how our cells age
item.description: Scientists have discovered that the body's cellular recycling system behaves very differently during aging than previously believed, with higher activity sometimes linked to worse physical health. A small study suggests that even gentle exercise could help restore more youthful cellular recycling patterns in older adults. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Rangers reimagine AI in wildlife monitoring
item.description: As workplaces around the world wrestle with integrating artificial intelligence into their operations, researchers and rangers in the heart of West Arnhem are successfully embracing this technology in conservation without compromising respect and knowledge. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: This tiny jurassic predator helped pave the way for the human brain
item.description: A 165-million-year-old fossil has revealed an extraordinary Jurassic predator that may help explain how mammals developed one of their most important evolutionary advantages. Although only 20 inches long, Megacauda sungei was a heavyweight among early mammal relatives, swimming through ancient waterways and hunting prey with specialized teeth. Its advanced swallowing anatomy reveals an early step toward the ability to safely nurse on milk, a key development in mammalian evolution. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: World's largest penguin colony loses its title after decline of more than 250,000 breeding pairs
item.description: Zavodovski, a volcanic island in Antarctica, is silently witnessing a shift in the local ecosystem. Known as home to the world's largest penguin colony, this island has long been under the watchful eye of scientists. One such study has now led to a bittersweet discovery. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: DNA recording system reveals how a single cell becomes a body
item.description: Scientists have traced the development of a mouse embryo from its first two cells to the formation of organs, using a remarkable DNA recording system that reveals the family history of individual cells. Their findings uncover how different cell types emerge on their own schedules and could help explain what goes wrong in birth defects, genetic disorders, and cancer. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Indonesia returns 20 green sea turtles to the ocean after Bali smuggling raid
item.description: Indonesian authorities on the tourist island of Bali released 20 protected green sea turtles back into the ocean Tuesday after they were found and seized on an empty boat seemingly abandoned by wildlife smugglers fleeing a police raid. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
item.description: Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: The secret to handling stress better may start at breakfast
item.description: Your daily routine could have a bigger impact on your ability to handle stress than you realize. A Binghamton University study of approximately 400 college students found that eating breakfast regularly, exercising, sleeping well, and taking fish oil were associated with greater psychological flexibility, which helps people adapt to stressful situations. Poor sleep and unhealthy eating habits, meanwhile, were linked to lower flexibility and resilience. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Cuando se agota nuestra batería social, necesitamos estar solos. La ciencia ha descubierto la otra cara de esa calma
item.description: Hay mucha gente que habla de "batería social" para referirse a la cantidad de tiempo que puede estar con otras personas conversando o haciendo planes diferentes. Pero llega un punto donde esta "batería" se agota y se necesita pasar un tiempo en soledad, desconectado del mundo, para poder recargarla. Y aquí la ciencia confirma que es cierto que este "efecto calmante" es real, pero viene con una factura oculta en nuestro estado de ánimo. El precio de la calma. Para entender cómo nos afecta realmente pasar tiempo con nosotros mismos, un equipo de investigadores publicó un estudio donde hizo un… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: Para dejar de pescar tantos peces estamos pescando peces que dan de comer a otros peces, y la devastadora factura final está llegando a Canarias
item.description: Una investigación llevada a cabo por un grupo de investigadores internacionales junto a de Outlaw Ocean Project ha llegado a una conclusión muy sencilla: el gran invento para frenar la sobrepesca se está comiendo su propia promesa. Décadas después, la industria ha construido una paradoja digna de unos Juegos del Hambre bajo el mar. Millones de peces salvajes terminan triturados y convertidos en alimento para otros peces que después llegan a nuestros supermercados. Y muchas veces la ruta termina de forma drástica en Canarias. La promesa para salvar los océanos. El trabajo parte de datos que… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: Nasa’s Perseverance rover on Mars breaks record for off-planet driving
item.description: Nasa’s robotic Perseverance rover has now driven farther than any other vehicle on the surface of any world other than Earth, racking up 45.2km (28.1 miles) since arriving on Mars in 2021, the US space agency said on Tuesday. The car-sized, six-wheeled rover reached the milestone 5½ years into its mission to explore if conditions conducive to microbial life ever existed on Earth’s neighbour. In doing so, it is visiting some of the ‌most ancient terrain ever encountered in the solar... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Reuters

item.title: China-US astronomy team may have found possible relic of a recent ‘gold factory’
item.description: A mysterious glow of high-energy light in our Milky Way galaxy could be the remains of an extremely rare cosmic “gold factory”, according to a new study by Chinese and US researchers. The collision of two orbiting neutron stars – dead stars so dense that a teaspoon of their matter would weigh a billion tonnes – may have shone as brightly as Jupiter in the sky, they wrote in a paper posted last week on the preprint server arXiv, which has yet to be peer-reviewed. The violent smash spewed out... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Ling Xin

item.title: Scientists uncover a hidden map of the brain with 539 distinct regions
item.description: Scientists have uncovered a hidden layer of organization in the brain by creating the first detailed 3D map of its lipids, the fatty molecules essential for brain structure and communication. By analyzing millions of measurements from mouse brains, researchers identified 539 distinct chemical zones, revealing patterns and boundaries that traditional brain maps have missed. Surprisingly, even white matter, once thought to be relatively uniform, contains a complex patchwork of chemically distinct regions. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Physicists discover “astonishing” property of light that defies expectations
item.description: Scientists have uncovered a surprising hidden ability of light that allows it to develop spinning, twisting behavior as it travels through empty space, without special lenses, mirrors, or materials. Researchers discovered that light’s internal geometry can naturally produce left- and right-handed patterns, challenging long-standing assumptions about how light behaves. By carefully arranging a beam’s structure, scientists can control where and how these spinning patterns emerge, unlocking a new way to manipulate light. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.description: A century of recipes published in the magazine Good Housekeeping reveals how the variety of seafood presented to U.K. readers has "narrowed," new research shows. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Snakebites are a far bigger problem than we knew: new study maps the hidden dangers
item.description: Not every snakebite injects venom. When venom enters the body, however, it can cause snake envenoming. This is a potentially fatal condition that mostly affects poor rural communities across tropical and subtropical regions where people don't have easy access to medical care. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists just gave the powerhouses of our cells a high-tech upgrade
item.description: Scientists have created a new coating for mitochondria that preserves their ability to produce energy, potentially opening the door to new treatments for diseases involving these tiny cellular powerhouses. The technology could one day help transfer healthy mitochondria into damaged cells, although its effectiveness in transplantation remains unproven. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Europe's new Sentinel-3C satellite just sent back spectacular images of Earth
item.description: Europe's Sentinel-3C satellite has returned breathtaking images of Earth just two weeks after launch, revealing the snowy Alps, frozen Arctic islands, and brilliant turquoise Caribbean waters. Its first measurements also show promising results for tracking rising seas, melting ice sheets, and other changes reshaping our planet. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Stabilizing a simple amino acid opens a path to biodegradable sensors
item.description: The humble amino acid glycine—the simplest of all amino acids—is everywhere. The human body produces it, and it helps make up our skin, bones and ligaments. It's found in meats like beef and has even been discovered in comets returned from outer space. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Gravity and quantum information linked through a derivation of Einstein's equations
item.description: Recent research shows that gravity and quantum information are deeply connected and that the shape of spacetime can be traced back to the way information is stored in quantum fields. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New research traces the origins and human impact of Britain's largest medieval lead industry through ancient teeth
item.description: The first definitive evidence of when post-Roman lead production began in one of Europe's largest medieval lead-producing regions, the Derbyshire Peak District in central England, has been uncovered by archaeologists after centuries of mining had erased much of the archaeological evidence. The work has been published in Antiquity. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Magnetic sculpting transforms single-source fields into predetermined shapes with mathematical precision
item.description: Magnetic fields are invisible yet essential components in technologies ranging from MRI scanners and particle accelerators to atomic clocks and future quantum computers. Each of these applications requires magnetic fields with specific shapes and properties. Today, creating such tailored magnetic fields requires researchers and engineers to design specialized, carefully optimized magnets or large systems of coils for each individual application—a complex and resource-intensive process. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists find a hidden problem with endless smartphone scrolling
item.description: Excessive smartphone use may be taking a hidden toll on the brain and body, with heavy scrolling linked to poorer memory, reduced attention, disrupted sleep, and potential balance problems. Researchers found that weak self-control and fear of missing out, rather than personality alone, are key factors behind problematic phone use. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Bacterial antiviral defense suggests ancient link to human chromosome protection
item.description: A new antiviral defense system discovered by Columbia scientists could be adapted in the future into a gene editor that slows down aging in our cells and improves cancer therapies. At the same time, the discovery also sheds light on an ancient event in evolution that may have helped set the stage for the emergence of higher organisms. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Electoral integrity under pressure as elections faced persistent threats in 2025
item.description: Elections across the world faced a wide range of pressures on electoral integrity in 2025, from violence and misinformation and disinformation to electoral management malfunctions, cyberattacks and natural hazards, according to a new report. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Nanostructure-assisted ultrasound shows potential for Parkinson's treatment
item.description: Parkinson's disease (PD) is one of the most common neurological disorders associated with later life, and its prevalence rises sharply with age. It affects the brain systems that control movement, often causing tremor, stiffness, slowness and problems with balance, all of which can reduce independence and quality of life in older adults. The condition is mainly linked to the gradual loss of dopamine-producing nerve cells. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Chemical disorder gives new ceramic film magnetic properties for potential low-power electronics
item.description: A material thinner than a human hair may foster faster computing devices that demand less energy and store more data, according to a multi-institutional team led by researchers in the Penn State College of Earth and Mineral Sciences. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Your gut bacteria could be changing how many calories you absorb
item.description: Scientists have developed a model showing that gut bacteria play a surprisingly important role in how many calories we absorb, meaning food labels may not tell the full story. In a controlled study, people eating a high-fiber diet absorbed about 116 fewer calories per day than those eating a typical Western diet, without feeling hungrier. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: From nonmagnetic to magnetic: A 2D semiconductor with electrically tunable magnetism
item.description: Researchers from the National University of Singapore (NUS), in collaboration with scientists from institutions in Switzerland, the Czech Republic and Germany, have demonstrated a way to introduce magnetism into an otherwise nonmagnetic two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor and subsequently control its magnetic properties using an electrical voltage. The findings, published in Science Advances, establish a new platform for investigating electrically controllable magnetism in atomically thin materials, with potential implications for future spintronic technologies. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Data-driven cricket ratings could reveal undervalued batters and bowlers through peer comparisons
item.description: An analytical method could help high-level cricket franchises make more informed decisions about player recruitment, retention and team selection, according to research published in the International Journal of Services and Operations Management. The approach uses data envelopment analysis (DEA) to compare efficiency using multiple inputs and outputs. In the world of cricket, this means assessing players against their peers rather than relying on individual statistics. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Reinforced vertebrae allow plunge-diving seabirds to survive high-speed impact
item.description: A northern gannet scans the sea for fish from 100 feet (30 meters) in the air. Upon seeing a school, it pitches its body into a nosedive, somehow breaking the surface at 70 miles per hour (113 kilometers per hour) without breaking its neck. This daring maneuver seems to defy the laws of nature, but it's standard hunting behavior for plunge-diving seabirds. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists uncover the 2.3-billion-year-old secret that helped keep Earth habitable
item.description: Scientists may have solved a 2.3-billion-year-old mystery about how Earth maintained enough oxygen to support life. Ancient rocks reveal that phosphorus recycling in the oceans created a self-sustaining cycle that helped keep oxygen levels high, even as the planet underwent dramatic environmental changes. The discovery challenges assumptions about Earth's early atmosphere and raises new questions about why complex life took so long to emerge. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Global satellite data reveal widening recovery gap between urban and rural vegetation
item.description: A global study has revealed a striking divergence in how urban and rural vegetation respond to climate stress. The study was led by Jin Wu from the School of Biological Sciences, Faculty of Science, and professor Yuyu Zhou from the Department of Geography, Faculty of Social Sciences, at The University of Hong Kong (HKU), with Dr. Zhengfei Guo as the first author. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Cholesterol-linked drug boosts gene-targeting potency in early findings
item.description: Nucleic acid therapeutics, such as antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), have emerged as promising platforms for treating a variety of previously hard-to-treat diseases, including neurological diseases. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Vapor-based method creates ultralight aerogels without conventional liquid-based chemistry
item.description: Researchers at National Taiwan University (NTU), working across the College of Engineering, College of Medicine and National Taiwan University Hospital (NTUH), have developed a new method for producing aerogels, introducing what they describe as the world's first purely gaseous-born aerogel fabrication platform. The study is published in Nature Communications. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists find a surprising genetic twist behind octopus intelligence
item.description: The remarkable intelligence of octopuses, squid, and cuttlefish may trace back to an ancient reshuffling of their DNA that created new connections between genes. Scientists discovered that these changes in the genome's 3D structure may have helped drive the evolution of their unusually complex nervous systems. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: High-speed microscopy captures sugar-building enzymes forming rigid pairs and flexible assemblies
item.description: From a rigid molecular pair to flexible assemblies with moving domains, the enzymes that build sugar chains display strikingly different behaviors. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Oil company wins tenders in Channel Country with supply to stay in Australia
item.description: An Australian oil boss says any fossil fuels taken from a new location in Queensland's Channel Country will stay in Australia, but it could take years before oil or gas flows. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Crispian Yeomans

item.title: Baby tooth places macaques in northern Germany more than 300,000 years ago
item.description: A research team from the Senckenberg Centre for Human Evolution and Palaeoenvironment at the University of Tübingen and Leiden University in the Netherlands has examined a tooth from the Schöningen archaeological site in Lower Saxony. The study was published in Quaternary Environments and Humans. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Water-based process turns wood industry byproduct into carbon nanofibers for sodium-ion batteries
item.description: A new study led by researchers at the University of Limerick (UL) has identified a new battery material from a renewable wood industry byproduct that could help reduce reliance on scarce and expensive materials. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New light-emitting organic materials could enable deep-tissue bioimaging
item.description: Researchers at the University of St Andrews have identified the first examples of a new class of advanced organic semiconductor materials that could one day be used as bioimaging agents, opening up new possibilities for deep-tissue imaging. The study, published in Nature Communications, was led by the Zysman-Colman group in the School of Chemistry at the University of St Andrews in collaboration with the Pal group at Durham University. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Tiny fossils reveal a missing chapter of ocean life after Snowball Earth
item.description: A rare assemblage of micro- and macro-fossils found in a roadside outcrop in South China, featuring thin ribbons, branching shapes and a tiny balloon on a stalk, offers a glimpse of marine life after one of Earth's most extreme ice ages. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New study finds the staffing structure of an audit office improves outcomes
item.description: Audit firms rely on partners to oversee audits and client relationships; managers to supervise teams and projects; and staff to perform much of the day-to-day work. The more audit partners and managers are involved in supervising and reviewing audit engagements, the better the audits tend to be, according to new research from the University at Buffalo School of Management. Fuente: Phys.org.
